title: Enterprise Onboarding, Escalation, Integration & QBR Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended processes and templates for enterprise customer onboarding, integration handoff, escalation procedures, known-issues/workarounds, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) / health-check materials. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and on-call SREs involved in customer activation and ongoing health.

Scope and audience:
- Applies to all enterprise customers (Dedicated + Private deployments), and self-serve customers transitioning to sales-assisted support.
- Owners: Customer Success for onboarding & QBR; Solutions Engineering for integration; Support & SRE for incident/escalation handling.

Key objectives:
- Achieve Time-to-Value (TTV) targets: first successful API call in < 48 hours for hosted pilot; baseline workload deployed in < 10 business days for Dedicated/Private.
- Maintain SLA-driven availability and response times (see "SLOs and escalation" below).
- Provide consistent QBR artifacts: usage/cost, latency percentiles, error rate, and model quality regressions.

Prerequisites (customer-facing and internal):
- Signed contract with onboarding plan and primary contacts (Technical Lead, Security Lead, Procurement).
- Customer workspace in Console provisioned, billing enabled, and API key created.
- For Dedicated/Private: network connectivity checklist completed (VPN/VPC peering, firewall rules, NAT/Gateway, KMS), and on-prem packaging pre-approved.

Onboarding Playbook (step-by-step):
1. Kickoff (Day 0)
   - Attendees: CS Lead, SE, Customer Technical Lead, Security Lead, Account Exec.
   - Agenda: goals, success metrics, timeline, security requirements, initial dataset and throughput expectations.
   - Deliverable: Onboarding Plan doc (shared confluence page + project tracker).

2. Provisioning & Access (Day 1-2)
   - Actions: Create Console project, grant IAM roles (CS_read, SE_integration, Customer_admin), verify API key.
   - Security: Exchange required audit/logging settings and KMS keys for Private.
   - Verification: Customer can perform a sample generation and embedding call.

3. Integration & Validation (Day 2-7)
   - SE runs integration checklist (see Integration Checklist below).
   - Perform load test up to customer baseline QPS with tracing enabled.
   - Validate latency p50/p95 against expectations and document any model selection/quantization tradeoffs.

4. Acceptance & Training (Day 7-10)
   - Deliver runbooks for common troubleshooting, embedding maintenance, and rollback instructions.
   - Run a training session for customer engineering and product teams.
   - Final acceptance sign-off captured in Onboarding Plan.

Integration Checklist (minimum required items):
- API connectivity verified (curl sample request)
- Authentication and key rotation instructions provided
- Network egress/ingress rules validated (for Dedicated/Private)
- Expected request patterns documented (sequence length, batch sizes, embedding call frequency)
- Observability hooks installed: tracing header, request IDs, and metrics export endpoints
- Performance baseline captured: p50, p95 latency, errors per 1k requests, tokens per second
- Cost estimate for steady-state and burst scenarios provided

Sample curl verification snippet:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"Hello world"}'

SLOs and escalation matrix:
- SLO targets (applies to Hosted and Dedicated; Private customers may set custom SLOs in contract):
  - Availability: 99.95% monthly
  - Error rate: < 0.5% (5xx) per 1k requests
  - Latency: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 300ms for generation toy workloads; product workloads may have higher thresholds defined in Onboarding Plan
- Support response targets (tiered):
  - Sev 1 (production outage, all customers impacted or critical path blocked): 15 min acknowledge, 1 hour initial remediation plan, 4 hour target mitigation
  - Sev 2 (degraded performance impacting SLAs): 30 min acknowledge, 4 hour remediation plan
  - Sev 3 (functional but reduced experience, non-urgent): 4 business hours acknowledge, next-business-day remediation plan

Escalation Playbook (roles and steps):
1. Identification
   - Support receives alert via PagerDuty/Slack with runbook link and firing alert.
   - Triage: Support checks dashboards (Console -> Route metrics, infra health, GPU utilization), and determines severity.

2. Initial Containment (Support engineer)
   - Actions: Restart relevant service (if safe), scale burst pool, apply fallback routing to lower-cost/compatible model variant.
   - Communication: Post incident acknowledgement in customer slack/channel and update incident tracker.

3. On-call SRE / Runtime Owner involvement
   - If issue persists after containment window (30-60 minutes), page on-call SRE and Runtime Owner.
   - SRE runs profiling playbook: check kernel errors, memory/GPU OOM, queue length, and KV cache health.

4. Engineering Escalation
   - If root cause likely in code path (kernel/scheduler/serialization), escalate to eng-serving-runtime and assign a CR (critical repair) with owner.
   - If customer-facing regression (quality), engage Research/Applied ML for model/quantization rollback.

5. Executive Notification
   - For Sev1 incidents impacting SLAs, notify account exec and CS leadership within 2 hours with cadence updates.

Escalation matrix table (text):
- Events -> Primary -> Secondary -> Tertiary
- API outage -> Support -> On-call SRE -> Eng-serving-runtime
- Latency spike -> Support -> Performance on-call -> Eng-serving-runtime
- Model quality regression -> CS -> Research/Applied ML -> Product Lead

Communication & customer updates:
- Use dedicated incident channel for each customer (create at kickoff).
- Post an initial acknowledgement within response SLA and provide 30/60/120-minute updates until mitigation; then shift to hourly.
- Final incident report: summary, timeline, root cause, mitigation, next steps, and compensation/credits (if applicable).

Known Issues and Workarounds (select examples):
1. Issue: Intermittent 503s during high tail latency (observed in sequence lengths > 4k)
   Workaround: Temporarily route to a quantized model variant with smaller KV cache and limit per-request sequence length to 2k. Engineering follow-up: profiling ticket to optimize attention kernels.
2. Issue: Client-side embedding mismatch after SDK upgrade
   Workaround: Pin SDK to previous minor version and clear embedding cache. Provide SDK diff and release notes.
3. Issue: TLS handshake failures with older customer firewall configurations
   Workaround: Confirm TLS 1.2+ support; suggest customer update cipher suites and allow SNI. Provide network packet capture template for diagnostics.

Known-issues table (text columns):
- ID | Symptom | Impact | Workaround | Assigned owner
- KI-2026-012 | 503s on long sequences | High | Route to quantized variant, limit seq len | eng-serving-runtime
- KI-2025-089 | Embedding drift after SDK 2.3.0 | Medium | Roll back SDK, clear cache | eng-developer-experience
- KI-2026-033 | TLS handshake errors | Low | Update firewall cipher list | customer-success

Support process & runbooks (links and entry points):
- Primary support channel: customer slack + support portal ticketing.
- Oncall: PagerDuty rotations are documented in eng-sre/runbooks.
- Runbooks to include: API-503-troubleshoot, latency-profiling-playbook, model-rollback-procedure, cache-clear-and-warmup.

Runbook excerpt: API-503-troubleshoot (quick steps)
1. Confirm alert (Console -> error rates) and correlate with infra metrics (GPU queue depth).
2. Check recent deploys (CI/CD pipeline, release-notes).
3. If queue depth > threshold (e.g., 80%), scale burst pool or apply throttling.
4. If kernel OOM observed, collect profile and escalate to runtime team.

Health checks and QBR materials (templates and cadence):
- Weekly health check (CS & SE): automated health digest sent to customer with:
  - Monthly usage summary (tokens, embedding units, routes used)
  - Latency p50/p95, error rates, and top error types
  - Cost delta vs. forecast and suggestions from Redwood Optimize
  - Open issues and action items with owners and ETA

- Quarterly Business Review (QBR) agenda (template):
  1. Executive summary & wins (5 min)
  2. Usage & cost review (10 min)
  3. Performance & reliability (10 min)
  4. Quality & model regressions (10 min)
  5. Roadmap & feature requests (10 min)
  6. Action items & next steps (5 min)

QBR artifacts checklist:
- Exported metrics dashboard (Console links) for the quarter
- Top 10 prompts/flows by cost and latency
- Regression tests/evals results if any model changes were made
- Recommendations from Redwood Optimize (batching, quantization, routing)

Templates: Health Check email subject/body (sample)
Subject: Redwood Health Digest  <Customer>  Week of YYYY-MM-DD
Body: Hello <Customer Team>,
Attached: usage.csv, latency_report.pdf
Highlights:
- Tokens: 1.2M ( 7% vs prior)
- p95 latency: 210ms (within expected)
- Incidents: 0 critical, 1 minor (resolved)
Action items:
- SE to validate a prompt-optimization to reduce token usage (owner: SE, ETA: 2 weeks)

Operational metrics to track for each account (recommended):
- Tokens per day, Embedding units per day
- p50/p95/p99 latency per route/model
- 5xx error rate per 1k requests
- Cache hit ratio (prefix/KV)
- Cost per 1M tokens per route

Ownership and roles (contact matrix):
- Customer Success Lead: primary relationship, QBR owner, contract renewals.
- Solutions Engineer: technical integration, runbook author, post-onboarding support.
- Support Engineer: first-line triage and communications.
- On-call SRE / Runtime Owner: incident ownership for serving runtime issues.
- Research / Applied ML: model quality regressions and evaluation harnesses.

Appendix: common CLI/commands and artifacts
- Sample trace URL: https://console.redwood.ai/projects/<project-id>/traces/<trace-id>
- Collecting logs (example):
  - kubectl -n redwood logs svc/runtime --since=1h | gzip > runtime-logs-<ts>.gz
  - python tools/collect_profiles.py --start 2026-03-01T12:00:00Z --end 2026-03-01T12:30:00Z --output /tmp/profile.tar.gz

- Escalation contact roster (example formatting; fill at kickoff):
  - Customer primary technical: name / email / phone
  - CS Lead: Aisha Patel / aisha@redwood.ai / +1-415-555-0172
  - On-call SRE: see eng-sre/pagerduty schedule link
